Part of Speech: loanword) + 이/가 (subject marker) + 쌓이다 (to pile up — passive of 쌓다)
column7: If you keep doing overtime your stress builds up.

Etymology: 스트레스 (stress) + 를 (object marker) + 풀다 (to untie / release)
Sentence Translation: I relieve stress by listening to music.

Etymology: 전화 (電話 telephone) + 를 (object marker) + 걸다 (to hang / initiate a connection)
Example Sentence: 밤 늦게 친구한테 전화를 걸면 안 돼요.
Sentence Translation: You shouldn't call your friends late at night.

Etymology: 전화 (電話 telephone) + 를 (object marker) + 끊다 (to cut / sever)
Sentence Translation: After hanging up on my parents I cried.

English: to shout / to let out a scream
Etymology: 소리 (sound / voice) + 를 (object marker) + 지르다 (to let out / to yell)
Sentence Translation: It's fine to just scream your lungs out at a norebang.

English: to muster energy / to cheer up
Etymology: 힘 (strength / energy) + 을 (object marker) + 내다 (to bring out / produce)
Example Sentence: 한번 울고 나면 다음에 더 힘을 낼 수 있어요.
Sentence Translation: After a good cry you can muster more energy next time.

English: to not let go of the microphone (mic hog)
Etymology: 마이크 (microphone) + 를 (object marker) + 놓다 (to put down / let go) + -지 않다 (negation)
Example Sentence: 노래방 꼴불견 1위는 마이크를 절대 놓지 않는 사람이에요.
Sentence Translation: The number one norebang nuisance is the person who never lets go of the mic.

English: to pull a blanket over oneself / to wrap up in a duvet
Etymology: 이불 (blanket / duvet) + 을 (object marker) + 뒤집어 쓰다 (to flip and wear — 뒤집다 to flip + 쓰다 to wear / cover)
Example Sentence: 혼자 이불을 뒤집어 쓰고 노래를 불렀어요.
Sentence Translation: I pulled the blanket over my head and sang alone.

English: to turn on a backing track and leave it running
Etymology: 노래 (song) + 반주 (伴奏 musical accompaniment) + 를 (object marker) + 켜다 (to turn on) + -아 놓다 (do and leave in that state)
Example Sentence: 컴퓨터로 노래 반주를 켜 놓고 연습했어요.
Sentence Translation: I turned on a backing track on my computer and practiced.

English: to chatter / to have a good gossip
Etymology: 수다 (chatter / small talk) + 를 (object marker) + 떨다 (to shake / scatter — here: to let loose)
Example Sentence: 친구들하고 수다를 떨면서 스트레스가 많이 풀렸어요.
Sentence Translation: I relieved a lot of stress chatting away with friends.

English: to gain weight / to put on weight
Etymology: 살 (flesh / body fat) + 이 (subject marker) + 찌다 (to gain weight)
Example Sentence: 스트레스를 받으면 맛있는 걸 많이 먹어서 살이 쪄요.
Sentence Translation: When I'm stressed I eat a lot of good food and gain weight.

English: to cause trouble / harm to someone
Etymology: 피해 (被害 harm / damage suffered) + 를 (object marker) + 주다 (to give)
Example Sentence: 다른 사람들한테 피해를 주지 말고 그냥 자요.
Sentence Translation: Don't cause trouble for others — just sleep.

Etymology: 그리움 (longing / yearning — from 그립다 to miss someone) + 이 (subject marker) + 생기다 (to arise / come into being)
Example Sentence: 부모님이 보고 싶을 때 그리움이 생겨서 스트레스가 돼요.
Sentence Translation: When I miss my parents a longing arises and it becomes stress.

Etymology: 힘 (strength) + 이 (subject marker) + 생기다 (to arise / come into being)
Example Sentence: 한번 울고 나면 정말 힘이 생겨요.
Sentence Translation: After a good cry you really feel strength welling up.

English: to treat someone well while you have them / don't take someone for granted
Etymology: 있을 때 (while [they] are here — 있다 to exist + -을 때 when) + 잘 하다 (to do well / treat well)
Example Sentence: 있을 때 잘 해요. 후회하지 말고.
Sentence Translation: Treat me well while I'm here. Don't regret it later.
